error_noHome: Home directory not found (HOME is not set)
error_invalidId: Invalid key ID “{id}” (allowed are a–z, 0–9, - and _)
error_signWithoutEmail: Key “{id}” is to sign commits but has no e-mail of its own
error_duplicateAlias: Host “{host}” already belongs to another key
error_duplicateHost: {hostname} is already part of this key
error_toolMissing: Program “{tool}” not found – is it installed?
error_stalePlan: The configuration changed since the preview: {path}
error_stalePreview: The configuration changed since the preview – please reload the preview
error_invalidPath: Invalid folder “{path}” – please start it with / or ~/
error_hostKeyChanged: The host key of {host} is not the confirmed one – connection aborted. Check whether the server was reinstalled.
doctor_dolphin_unknown_detail: To check, open sftp://<alias> in Dolphin: it should connect with the key from Keybund, without a password.
doctor_dolphin_old: Dolphin does not see Keybund's config (libssh {version})
doctor_dolphin_old_detail: libssh before 0.10.2 does not understand ~ in Include – sftp:// in Dolphin then does not use the key from Keybund. Fix: write the Include with the full path.
doctor_sshDir_bad_detail: Others may write to ~/.ssh and could swap keys or the config.
doctor_sshConfigPerms_ok: ssh configs belong to you and only you can write them
doctor_sshConfigPerms_bad: ssh does not read this config
doctor_sshConfigPerms_bad_detail: ssh refuses a config that belongs to someone else or that others may write to (“Bad owner or permissions”) – then no Host block applies, Keybund's included.
doctor_keyPerms_bad: Private keys with too open permissions
doctor_sshInclude_ok: The Include is at the top of ~/.ssh/config
doctor_sshInclude_notTop: The Include is not at the top
doctor_sshInclude_notTop_detail: In ~/.ssh/config it is below a Host block and only applies to that one.
doctor_gitInclude_notLast: Keybund is no longer at the end of ~/.gitconfig
doctor_gitInclude_notLast_detail: What comes after it (e.g. from git config --global) overrides the settings of your keys.
doctor_gitEnv_sshCommand: GIT_SSH_COMMAND is set in {origin} (“{value}”). Git then uses this command in every repository instead of the key from Keybund. Remove the line and log in again or open a new terminal.
doctor_gitEnv_config: {name} points to {value} in {origin} – Git then does not read ~/.gitconfig with Keybund's include. Remove the line and log in again or open a new terminal.
doctor_agent_missing_detail: SSH_AUTH_SOCK is not set or the agent is not running. Keys with a passphrase are asked for on every connection.
doctor_agent_missing_detail_macos: On macOS, launchd starts the agent at login. Here SSH_AUTH_SOCK is not set – usually a line in the shell profile overrides it. Keys with a passphrase are then asked for on every connection.
doctor_agent_terminalOnly: ssh-agent only runs in the terminal
doctor_agent_terminalOnly_detail: Your shell profile starts an agent ({socket}) that programs from the menu – Keybund, Dolphin, the IDE – do not see. They ask for the passphrase every time. Better: use the desktop's agent (KDE: ssh-agent in the autostart settings, GNOME: gnome-keyring).
doctor_addKeys_missing_detail: Keys with a passphrase are asked for on every use: {files}. Write the configs again.
doctor_sshConfig_old_detail: It was taken over into Keybund but still offers {key} – a login can then succeed with the wrong key. Remove it.
doctor_sshConfig_global_detail: {key} is offered in addition to the key from Keybund – a login can succeed with the wrong key. Take it over into Keybund with “Take over existing SSH config”, then remove it.
doctor_sshConfig_duplicate_detail: Keybund writes this Host block itself, the old one can go.
doctor_globalIdentity_detail: {files} is offered on every connection, also to the hosts of your keys. If it is in the ssh-agent, it comes first – the login can then succeed with the wrong account. Better list it only in the Host blocks that need it.
doctor_ownSshCommand: The default key replaces your core.sshCommand
doctor_ownSshCommand_detail: ~/.gitconfig sets “{command}”, but outside the Git folders the default key “{name}” applies. Remove the line or unset the default.
doctor_keyAge: The key of “{name}” is {years} years old
doctor_keyAge_detail: Create a new key and remove the old one at the provider.
probe_noPassphrasePrompt: Could not ask for the passphrase – load the key once with ssh-add
probe_loggedIn_noCommand: Login successful – but the server runs no commands (exit status {code})
probe_keyUnknown_server: The server does not know this key
probe_hostKeyChanged: The host key of {host} has changed – check first, then remove it with ssh-keygen -R
probe_hostKeyUnconfirmed: The host key of {host} is not confirmed yet
probe_otherKey_as: Logged in as {account}, but with {key} instead of this key
probe_otherKey: Logged in, but with {key} instead of this key
step_hostKeyOk: The host key is known and matches – it is the right server
step_rejected: The server does not know this key
step_noMoreKeys: No further key to offer – login failed
step_hostNotFound: Hostname not found – a typo, or no network?
step_hostKeyFailed: Host key not confirmed or changed – connection aborted
which_keyFileMissing: The key file {path} does not exist.
which_localOverride: The folder belongs to the key “{name}”, but git uses another key. Check the repository's local config.
which_noSshCommand: Git sets no core.sshCommand here – ssh picks the key itself.
which_notARepo: Not a Git repository: applies to all repositories in this folder.
which_defaultApplies: The folder belongs to no key, the default key applies.
which_noKey: The folder belongs to no key and there is no default key.
which_gitSshCommand: GIT_SSH_COMMAND is set ({origin}) and overrides Keybund: git uses “{value}”.
which_gitConfigGlobal: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL points to {value} ({origin}) – ~/.gitconfig with Keybund is not read.
which_triesKeys: ssh tries {n} keys one after the other.
which_folderDecides: For Git repositories the folder decides, not the host ({host} is used by {names}).
import_needsFolder: Another key is already the default – this one only applies with a Git folder.
import_becomesDefault: Becomes the default key: applies to {host} in all folders without a key of their own
import_severalIdentityFiles: Several IdentityFile entries – the first one is taken over
install_denied: Login to {host} failed – the password or a key that is already there is needed
install_noAskpass: No password dialog available – run `keybund install-key` in a terminal
hostKey_declined: Host key not confirmed – no connection was made.
toast_savedDetail: Git and ssh use it from now on.
toast_pubkeyCopied: Public key copied to the clipboard
sidebar_cloneHint: Clones a repository straight into the folder of the matching key
sidebar_doctorHint: Checks that ssh and Git are set up correctly
probe_details: Details: what happened during the test
probe_noSteps: ssh did not report any details.
probe_tryYourself: Try it yourself in a terminal (with -v for all details):
hostKey_explain: The server identifies itself with this host key. Compare the fingerprint with the server (ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub) or with what your hoster shows. Only if it matches is it really your server.
howItWorks_keyText: A separate SSH key for each purpose – private, client A, NAS. The private part stays on your computer; the public one (“public key”) goes to GitHub, GitLab or the server.
howItWorks_rulesTitle: Rules instead of trial and error
howItWorks_rulesText: Keybund writes small rules into the config of Git and ssh: “repositories in ~/dev/client-a/ → key A”, “server nas → key B”. So no repository ever takes the wrong key by accident.
howItWorks_runsText: Git and ssh read these rules themselves. Keybund does not have to run for that – you work as usual in the terminal, the IDE or the file manager.

match.nPlural=one: {n} config file does not match your keys – was it changed outside Keybund?
match.nPlural=other: {n} config files do not match your keys – were they changed outside Keybund?

home_emptyText: Create a new key or take over the keys you already have in ~/.ssh.

match.nPlural=one: Your {file} has an entry with its own key that Keybund can take over.
match.nPlural=other: Your {file} has {n} entries with their own key that Keybund can take over.

home_allFine: All fine – Git and ssh pick the right key automatically.
home_unusedCard: Not used anywhere yet – open it and choose what for
newKey_errorNameChars: The name needs at least one letter or digit.
newKey_errorFileExists: {path} already exists – choose “Use an existing key” or another name.
newKey_intro: Give the key a name you recognise it by. What it is for – Git folders, GitHub, servers – you set right after.
newKey_namePlaceholder: e.g. Private, Client C or NAS
newKey_generateHint: recommended – a key of its own for this purpose
newKey_existingHint: a key that is already in ~/.ssh
newKey_passphraseHint: Protects the key if someone gets hold of your files. You type it once per session; after that the ssh-agent remembers the key.
newKey_commentHint: Stands at the end of the public key – it is how you recognise the key on GitHub or on the server.
which_intro: Enter a folder or host. Keybund shows what ssh and git really use there.
which_identitiesOnlyYes: yes, only this key is offered
which_forFolder: for git push, pull and fetch in this folder
doctorPage_intro: Checks permissions, include lines, the agent and whether all configs are up to date.
apply_intro: What you change in Keybund is written right away. These files still do not match your keys – usually because they were edited or deleted by hand. Keybund only writes its own files and one include line each in ~/.ssh/config and ~/.gitconfig; your files are backed up first.
clone_intro: includeIf does not apply yet when cloning – so Keybund clones directly with the matching key.
clone_noMatch: No key is set up for {host} – please pick one.
import_intro: Entries with their own key in {file} become keys in Keybund. The key files stay where they are.
import_nothingLeft: All taken over – nothing in ~/.ssh/config mixes with Keybund any more.

match.nPlural=one: All taken over: {n} key, old entries removed
match.nPlural=other: All taken over: {n} keys, old entries removed

import_doneHint: Git and ssh use Keybund's rules from now on. Best test the connection once on the key's page.
import_aliasHint: Alias: repositories with {alias} use this key. With a Git folder it also applies to {host} in that folder.
import_removeOld: Remove the old entries from ~/.ssh/config afterwards (recommended)
import_removeOldHint: As long as they are there, ssh offers their keys as well – a login can then succeed with the wrong key. A backup is made first (~/.ssh/config.keybund-backup).
import_cleanupText: Keybund covers these entries now. As long as they are there, ssh offers their keys as well. A backup is made first (~/.ssh/config.keybund-backup).
uninstall_intro: Removes everything Keybund wrote: the include lines in your ~/.ssh/config and ~/.gitconfig and Keybund's own files. Your keys in ~/.ssh stay as they are.
uninstall_donePurged: The list of your keys is deleted too – the key files in ~/.ssh stay.
uninstall_doneKept: Keybund still knows your keys – “Rewrite configs” sets everything up again.
uninstall_restore: Restore the originals from the backup
uninstall_restoreHint: ~/.ssh/config and ~/.gitconfig as before Keybund – also brings back entries that were taken over; your later changes to these files are lost.
uninstall_purge: Also delete Keybund's list of keys
uninstall_purgeHint: ~/.config/keybund/profiles.toml – keep it to set Keybund up again later.
uninstall_confirmText: Git will then no longer pick the key automatically. Your keys stay; the preview shows the changes.
settings_defaultLabel: Key for repositories outside your Git folders
settings_defaultHint: For all Git repositories that are in no key's Git folder, e.g. a quickly cloned repository in ~/Downloads. Without a default key ssh simply tries your keys.
settings_keysHint: You can take over a key Keybund does not know yet – or {link}.
settings_pathsHint: Keybund reads and writes these files. Your own ones (SSH, Git) only get one include line each.
settings_removeHint: Takes back all of Keybund's changes, with a preview. Your keys stay.
settings_license: License: GPL-3.0 · a commercial license is available via
settings_projectsDirHint: Keybund suggests Git folders here, e.g. {example}.
settings_knownHostsHint: ssh remembers how it recognises your servers. With this option that is kept in a file per key and goes away when the key is archived.
settings_absoluteIncludeHint: Instead of ~ in ~/.ssh/config – needed for Dolphin/KIO with libssh before 0.10.2 (the doctor reports it).
settings_languageHint: Error messages, the doctor and connection tests follow the chosen language. The command line is in German.
settings_themeHint: “Like the system” switches with the light or dark mode of your desktop.
usage_intro: Keybund tells Git and ssh when to use this key – after that everything happens automatically, even without Keybund running.
usage_defaultDetail: Git uses this key in all folders where no other key applies – e.g. for a quickly cloned repository.
usage_folderDetail: Git repositories in this folder (and all subfolders) use this key and your Git identity below.
usage_folderTile: All repositories in a folder, e.g. ~/dev/client-c/ – with their own name and e-mail in the commits.
usage_accountTile: GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket – Keybund helps you add the key there so you can push.
usage_serverTile: ssh, scp and sftp to a computer or an IP – also in sftp clients and file managers.
usage_orDefault: Or: use it as the default for Git (wherever no other key applies)
test_otherKeyText: ssh also offered {key} (from your ~/.ssh/config), and that is what logged in. Add this key at the provider and remove the old entry.
account_aliasDetail: Repositories with git@{alias}:… use this key ({host}). The key has to be in your {provider} account.
account_detail: For {provider} to recognise you, the key has to be in your account.
account_addKeyHint: Copy the public key and open the {provider} page to paste it
account_pasteHint: On the {provider} page choose “New SSH key”, paste it and save – logged in with the account for “{name}”.
account_signingHint: For signed commits add the same key there once more with “Key type: Signing Key”.
account_fixText: The key is not in your {provider} account yet. Copy the public key and paste it there under SSH keys – Keybund opens the page.
server_detail: ssh {name} connects to {target} – with this key, also scp, sftp and rsync.
server_installing: Logging in to {name} – enter the password if asked …
server_fixText: {name} does not know this key yet. Keybund adds it there like ssh-copy-id – the server asks for your password once.
folder_errorIdentity: Please enter a name and a valid e-mail.
folder_hint: Leave empty for {folder} – it is created if missing.
folder_identityHint: Suggested from ~/.gitconfig. For a client simply change the e-mail – it then only applies in this key's Git folders.
folder_providerHint: Then Keybund can help add the key there right away. Self-hosted? Later under “Git account”.
keyCard_notInAgentHint: The ssh-agent remembers the key after its first use – then nobody asks for the passphrase any more.
keyCard_intro: The public part (“public key”) goes to GitHub, GitLab or servers; the private part stays on your computer.
keyCard_show: Show public key, fingerprint and file
keyCard_explain: An SSH key has two parts: you hand the {public} (“public key”, below) to GitHub, GitLab or a server. The {private} {path} stays on your computer – with it ssh proves that it is you.
hostForm_serverAliasHint: With an alias you later just type ssh nas instead of ssh admin@192.168.1.5.
hostForm_accountAliasHint: An alias is only needed if you have several accounts with the same provider: then you clone with git@github-client:org/repo.
identity_globalApplies: This key has no Git folder. Your commits therefore use the global identity from ~/.gitconfig:
identity_globalMissing: This key has no Git folder. Your commits therefore use the global identity from ~/.gitconfig – but none is set there; Git asks for it with the first commit.
identity_ownViaFolder: A key gets an identity of its own, e.g. a client's e-mail, through a Git folder.
identity_intro: Name and e-mail in the commits of this key's Git folders. Empty means: as in ~/.gitconfig.
identity_invalidEmail: Please enter a valid e-mail address.
identity_signHint: Sign with this key – GitHub and GitLab then show the commits as “Verified” if the key is also registered there as a signing key.
identity_signNeedsEmail: For that the key needs an e-mail of its own.
manage_intro: Archiving retires the key: it moves to ~/.ssh/archive/ and the rules for Git and ssh are removed – e.g. when a client project ends.
manage_confirmText: The key moves to ~/.ssh/archive/; the rules for Git and ssh are removed right away. Remember to delete the key at GitHub & co. and on servers too.
manage_removeAtProvider: Remove the key at the provider: {url}
config_explainSsh: Tells ssh which key applies to which server or alias.
config_explainIndex: Tells Git which settings apply in which folder.
config_explainKey: Name, e-mail and key for Git in this key's folders.
config_archived: This key is archived: Keybund writes no rules for it any more; Git and ssh do not use it.
config_intro: This is how Git and ssh see this key. Keybund writes these files itself – you do not need to touch any of them. They show how Git and ssh know which key is in use.
which_unknownHost: No key knows this host – ssh tries its default keys.
